sections.title: The Cognitive Science of Conversation (PD)
sections.description: What makes a conversation "good"? How do we achieve the feeling of being "on the same page" with an interlocutor? This course explores the neurological and cognitive underpinnings of effective communication, equipping students with the scientific knowledge necessary to foster constructive dialogue. Drawing on cuttingedge research - including the work of Thalia Wheatley, Michael Frank, Carolyn Parkinson, and Robert Hawkins - the class investigates the social neuroscience and cognitive psychology of human connection. By analyzing primary literature on theory of mind, neural alignment, active listening, and the creation of shared meaning, students will translate up-to-date scientific insights into actionable strategies for navigating complex dialogues. Paideia program courses are open to all students, not just Paideia fellows.
